### 1 — Scene
A mixed buffet-style meal: a large roasted rib, a small slice of beef, a breaded fried chicken piece, and two sushi pieces.

### 2 — Vessel
A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- Roasted rib, apparently bone-in
- Small slice of cooked beef behind the rib
- Breaded fried chicken
- Crab-style sushi roll
- Fried/coated sushi roll

No separate sauce or dressing is visible. Frying oil is included in the fried foods’ energy densities.

### 4–6 — Area, volume, and weight
Coverage estimates count the exposed portions without double-counting overlaps.

| Item | Plate coverage | Area | Typical height | Gross volume | Density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bone-in rib | 17% | 90 cm² | 1.5 cm | 135 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 128 g including bone |
| Beef slice | 3% | 16 cm² | 1.3 cm | 21 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 20 g |
| Fried chicken | 5.5% | 29 cm² | 2 cm | 58 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 52 g |
| Crab-style sushi | 3% | 16 cm² | 2 cm | 32 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 29 g |
| Fried sushi | 2.8% | 15 cm² | 2 cm | 30 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 27 g |

Total coverage is **31.3%**, consistent with the substantial empty plate area. For the rib, I estimate approximately **35 g of bone**, leaving **93 g edible meat**. This is a bone exclusion, not an additional air/gap reduction.

### 7 — Energy
Using cooked, edible weights:

| Item | Edible grams | kcal/100 g | Estimated kcal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Rib meat | 93 | 320 | 298 |
| Beef slice | 20 | 250 | 50 |
| Fried chicken | 52 | 290 | 151 |
| Crab-style sushi | 29 | 160 | 46 |
| Fried sushi | 27 | 230 | 62 |
| **Total** | **221** | | **607** |

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **220 g edible food and 610 kcal** is plausible for this sparsely covered plate of mostly energy-dense meat and fried foods. Including the estimated rib bone, the plated contents weigh about **255 g**. Rib bone size and meat fat content are the largest uncertainties.
